standard_prerequisites.name: For a Nagata base and a finite type morphism with reduced source the normalization in the source is finite, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the normalization affine and finite over an affine base, so that the situation becomes a finite algebra over a Noetherian ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: The idempotence of the normalization, established earlier in the same chapter (and by a previous card of this lane), which lets the base be replaced by the normalization itself
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces to the case where base and normalization coincide.

standard_prerequisites.name: Prime avoidance together with the finiteness of the set of minimal primes of a Noetherian ring, and the description of the closure of the image of a closed subset as the specializations of its points
standard_prerequisites.use: Produce the element avoiding the minimal primes and show that the closure of the image of its vanishing locus avoids the point.

standard_prerequisites.name: The compatibility of integral closure with localization, and the characterization of a reduced ring as normal via its local behaviour, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Turn the equality between the ring and the integral closure in a localization into normality of the local ring at the point.

core_obligations: Reduce to an affine Noetherian situation: replace the base by an affine neighbourhood of the image of the point, use finiteness of the normalization in the Nagata case to write it as the spectrum of a finite algebra, and then replace the base by the normalization to assume base and normalization coincide (proof lines 14296-14303).

Choose an element avoiding the minimal primes: at the prime corresponding to the point pick an element in that prime but in no minimal prime of the ring, using prime avoidance and finiteness of the set of minimal primes (proof lines 14305-14309).

Show the vanishing locus of that element is irrelevant: its preimage in the source avoids all generic points by the choice of the element and avoids the point because the point is not in the image of the source; since only generic points specialize to a one-dimensional point, after shrinking the base the preimage is empty (proof lines 14310-14328).

Conclude normality: the element then becomes an invertible global function on the source, giving a factorization of the ring through its localization at that element, and because the base equals its normalization the ring is the integral closure of itself in that localization; localizing at the point and using that the localization of a one-dimensional reduced local ring at the element is a product of fields, the local ring is normal, hence a discrete valuation ring (proof lines 14329-14348).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a finite affine Noetherian situation where base and normalization coincide, pick an element avoiding minimal primes, and shrink so that its vanishing locus misses the source entirely (proof lines 14296-14328).
Read off that the ring is its own integral closure in the localization, localize at the point, and conclude normality hence the discrete valuation ring property (proof lines 14329-14348).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a finite type morphism with reduced source over a Nagata base, a one-dimensional point of the normalization lying outside the image of the source has discrete valuation ring (statement lines 14292-14302). The counted proof is a substantial argument: it reduces to a finite affine Noetherian situation with base equal to its normalization, uses prime avoidance to pick an element in the relevant prime but in no minimal prime, shows that the closure of the image of the vanishing locus of that element misses the point because only generic points specialize to a one-dimensional point, shrinks the base so that the vanishing locus disappears, and then reads normality of the local ring off the equality of the ring with its integral closure in a localization, using that the localization of a one-dimensional reduced ring is a product of fields (proof lines 14296-14348). It is H2: all reductions and the local computation are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard Nagata, prime avoidance and integral closure statements.
